outputs.L3:
The system is designed to suggest products or services that are better suited to each target person based on relevant human attributes.

The order processing system includes a mobile terminal used for entering orders, a register terminal that processes those orders, and a server connected to the register terminal. When an order is processed, the register terminal generates data that links the product or service provided with human attributes of the target person. These attributes may include gender, age, and ethnicity.

The server receives and accumulates this data from the register terminal. It then analyzes the accumulated information to determine which products or services are frequently used or selected for each combination of human attributes. Based on this analysis, the server generates recommendation data indicating products or services that are likely to be suitable for specific types of target persons.

The server then sends the analyzed recommendation data back to the register terminal. As a result, the register terminal can use the recommendation data to suggest appropriate products or services for each target person, improving the relevance and efficiency of the order processing system.

An order processing system is configured to collect and use customer attribute information in connection with products or services ordered by customers. The system includes, for example, a mobile terminal used by a staff member, a register terminal installed at a store or service location, and a server connected to the terminals through a communication network.

When a customer places an order, the staff member or operator may enter order information into the mobile terminal or the register terminal. The order information may identify one or more products or services selected by the customer. In addition to the order information, the system also receives or records attribute information relating to the customer. The attribute information may include, for example, gender, approximate age, age group, ethnicity, nationality, language, residence area, or other characteristics that may be useful for understanding customer preferences. The attribute information may be entered manually by an operator, selected from predefined categories, or obtained from another source connected to the system.

The mobile terminal or register terminal transmits the order information and the associated customer attribute information to the server. The server stores the received information in a database in a manner that links each ordered product or service with the corresponding customer attributes. For example, the server may store records indicating that customers belonging to a particular age group frequently ordered a certain menu item, that customers of a particular gender often selected a specific service, or that customers associated with a particular ethnicity or language group tended to choose certain products.

As more orders are processed, the server aggregates the stored data and analyzes ordering tendencies for each attribute group. The server may count the number of times each product or service has been ordered by customers having a particular attribute or combination of attributes. Based on the aggregated results, the server identifies products or services that are frequently used, frequently purchased, or otherwise popular among customers in each attribute group. The server may rank these offerings according to order frequency, sales volume, recency, or another evaluation criterion.

When a new customer is being served, the register terminal may receive or determine the customer’s attribute information and send it to the server, or may request recommendation information corresponding to that attribute information. In response, the server refers to the aggregated data and selects one or more products or services that have been frequently used by customers with the same or similar attributes. The server then transmits recommendation information to the register terminal.

The register terminal displays or otherwise presents the recommended products or services to the operator. The operator can then suggest the recommended offerings to the customer, or the recommendations may be displayed directly to the customer. In this way, the system enables products or services that are likely to match the preferences of a particular target person to be proposed at the time of ordering.

By associating order history with customer attributes and using aggregated ordering trends, the system supports more appropriate and effective recommendations. It can help improve customer satisfaction by presenting offerings that are suited to the customer’s characteristics, while also helping the store or service provider promote products or services more efficiently.

**Provided**

The word **“provided”** carries a sense of support, preparation, and possibility. When something is provided, a need is met, a resource is made available, or an opportunity is created. In everyday life, people rely on what is provided to learn, work, grow, and overcome challenges.

For example, education provides knowledge, guidance, and the skills needed for the future. Healthcare provides treatment and care when people are unwell. Technology provides faster communication, easier access to information, and new ways to solve problems. Even small acts of kindness, such as providing help to someone in need, can make a meaningful difference.

Being provided with the right tools or support can change the outcome of a situation. A student who is provided with books and encouragement may gain confidence. A community provided with clean water, safety, and opportunities can thrive. In this way, what is provided is not only about material things, but also about care, attention, and responsibility.

Ultimately, the idea of being “provided” reminds us of the importance of giving and receiving. It shows that progress often depends on the resources, support, and opportunities made available to people. When needs are recognized and properly provided for, individuals and communities are better able to succeed.

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a patent-style abstract for an order processing system that recommends products or services based on customer attributes such as gender, age, and ethnicity.
counterfactuals.output: An order processing system and method are provided for generating personalized product or service recommendations during an ordering workflow. The system receives customer attribute data, including one or more demographic attributes such as gender, age, and ethnicity, and stores the attribute data in association with customer profile information and transaction history. A recommendation engine compares the customer attribute data with product or service metadata, historical purchase patterns, inventory data, and predetermined business rules to identify candidate offerings relevant to the customer. The system ranks the candidate offerings according to a recommendation score and presents one or more recommended products or services through an ordering interface before, during, or after completion of an order. In some embodiments, the system applies privacy controls, consent verification, and fairness constraints to limit use of sensitive attributes and to reduce biased recommendation outcomes. The system may update recommendation models based on customer selections, completed transactions, and feedback to improve subsequent recommendations.
counterfactuals.label: cf_1

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a Japanese patent application abstract in English for a POS/order processing system where customer demographic attributes are associated with ordered items and analyzed on a server.
counterfactuals.output:
**Abstract**

An order processing system includes an order terminal configured to receive order information identifying one or more items ordered by a customer, an attribute input unit configured to acquire demographic attribute information of the customer, and a server communicably connected to the order terminal. The order terminal transmits, to the server, order data in which the ordered item information is associated with the demographic attribute information, including at least one of age, gender, customer segment, or group composition. The server stores the received order data in a database and performs analysis of ordering tendencies for each demographic attribute or combination of attributes. The server generates analysis information indicating relationships between customer attributes and ordered items, and outputs the analysis information to a management terminal or report generation unit. Accordingly, sales trends and customer preferences can be identified with improved accuracy, thereby supporting menu planning, inventory management, promotion planning, and store operation decisions.
counterfactuals.label: cf_3

counterfactuals.prompt: Describe an order processing system including mobile terminal 10, register terminal 11, and server 200, where the system accumulates first data and generates second data for frequently used products by human attributes.
counterfactuals.output:
An order processing system may include a **mobile terminal 10**, a **register terminal 11**, and a **server 200** connected through a network.

The **mobile terminal 10** is used by a customer or store staff to input or select products to be ordered. It may read product information, receive product selections, and transmit order-related information to the server 200.

The **register terminal 11** is installed at a store checkout area and processes payment or checkout operations. It may also acquire product purchase information, customer-related information, and transaction information, and send this information to the server 200.

The **server 200** manages order processing and data analysis. The server 200 accumulates **first data**, which includes information relating to ordered or purchased products and human attributes associated with users or customers. The human attributes may include, for example, age group, gender, occupation, residence area, family structure, or other customer classification information.

Based on the accumulated first data, the server 200 identifies products that are frequently used, ordered, or purchased for each human attribute category. The server 200 then generates **second data** indicating frequently used products by human attribute. For example, the second data may show which products are frequently purchased by customers in a particular age group or by customers having a particular lifestyle attribute.

The generated second data can be supplied to the mobile terminal 10 or register terminal 11 and used for product recommendation, order assistance, inventory planning, sales promotion, or display of frequently used products corresponding to the customer’s attributes. Thus, the system enables efficient order processing and attribute-based product recommendation using accumulated order and purchase history.
counterfactuals.label: cf_4

counterfactuals.prompt: Create a patent-like technical summary for a recommendation system that extracts frequently provided products or services for target persons by gender, age, and ethnic attribute using data sent from a register terminal to a server.
counterfactuals.output:
## Technical Summary

A recommendation system is provided for extracting and presenting frequently provided products or services associated with target persons classified by one or more demographic attributes, including gender, age, and ethnic attribute. The system includes a register terminal installed at a transaction location and a server communicatively connected to the register terminal through a network. The register terminal transmits transaction data, including information identifying a product or service provided to a person and demographic attribute information associated with the person, to the server. The server stores the transmitted data in a database, aggregates the data according to attribute categories, calculates provision frequencies of products or services for each category or combination of categories, and generates recommendation information based on the calculated frequencies.

In one embodiment, the register terminal includes an input unit for receiving transaction information, a demographic attribute acquisition unit for receiving or estimating demographic attributes of a target person, and a communication unit for transmitting the transaction information and demographic attribute information to the server. The demographic attribute information may include gender, age or age range, and ethnic attribute, provided that collection and processing are performed in accordance with applicable consent, privacy, and data protection requirements.

The server includes a receiving unit, a storage unit, an aggregation unit, a frequency calculation unit, and a recommendation generation unit. The receiving unit receives data from one or more register terminals. The storage unit stores the received data in association with product or service identifiers and demographic attribute identifiers. The aggregation unit groups transaction records by selected demographic attributes, such as gender, age range, ethnic attribute, or combinations thereof. The frequency calculation unit determines frequently provided products or services within each group by calculating counts, ratios, rankings, confidence values, or other statistical indicators. The recommendation generation unit extracts products or services having a frequency satisfying a predetermined threshold and outputs recommendation information corresponding to a selected target category.

In operation, when a register terminal records that a product or service has been provided to a person, the terminal transmits transaction data to the server. The server updates frequency information for the corresponding demographic group. When recommendation information is requested, the server identifies a target group based on input demographic attributes and retrieves products or services frequently provided to persons having the same or similar attributes. The server may then transmit the extracted recommendation information to the register terminal, a management terminal, or another authorized device.

The system may further include anonymization or pseudonymization processing so that personally identifiable information is not required for frequency extraction. The server may store demographic attributes as categorical or range-based values rather than direct identifiers. Access control, encryption, audit logging, consent management, and retention controls may be applied to protect sensitive demographic data. In addition, fairness controls may be implemented to prevent inappropriate exclusion, discriminatory treatment, or unlawful targeting based on protected attributes.

By aggregating transaction data received from register terminals and extracting products or services frequently provided to demographic groups, the system enables generation of statistically based recommendation information that can support inventory planning, service proposal generation, marketing analysis, or point-of-sale assistance while maintaining privacy and compliance safeguards.
